name: wordy+dup
text: Six weeks ago I pulled out of school and shut the fuck up. I didnt tell my friends and I didnt tell my peers. In order to be able to make progress at this point in time, it was decided by me that the best course of action would be to send a very large number of cold emails to founders. I lived in a tiny apartment with a blanket over the window to block the sun. It did not feel great. As I said before, it did not feel great at all. Then one morning a founder replied, we got on a call, and by the next day the deal was done. We raised over half a million dollars from Verdict Capital on October 12 to kill slop companies.

name: script run-on
text: So here is what actually happened. After the video blew up i kinda realized that school wasnt bringing me any closer to my goals. I had an audience, but no money. i wish i could say that i felt some sort of conviction, but honestly, it was stranger than anything i had ever experienced, and with every day that went by without results i couldnt help but question if i had made the right choice. Every day i woke up in my college apartment, made videos, and worked on my startup in a town where everyone around me studied. Nobody knew. Then one morning my cofounder sent out our 1068th investor email and someone finally replied.

name: long but clear
text: The committee reviewed the three proposals on Tuesday, asked each team for a revised budget by Friday, and plans to announce the winner at the all-hands meeting on the first of March. Because the venue had to be booked six months ahead and the caterer needed a final headcount, and since the speakers could only confirm after their visa interviews, which were themselves delayed twice, the date slipped to May 14. The new date works for everyone.
